title: advance-anchor cannot claim a superseded version's evidence head, so a rebind before its successor blocks every CI anchor (pilot finding 4)
description:

AdvanceAnchor and AnchorAdvanced carry only the unit name, and both _decide_advance_anchor and the fold resolve snapshot.evidence_head(unit_name) (src/vouch_mk2/core/decide.py:1130-1142 and 1828-1836), which is the current version's head. title: A merge replay drops the CI run claim of replayed anchor advances (pilot finding 3)
description:
Third D-24 pilot finding (activity_tracker_portal, 2026-10-16).

Setup: two feature branches from one base, PR #37 (receipt-bound-delivery@1) and PR #40 (notify-operator-conditions@1), each recorded Vouch transitions. PR #37 merged to main, and main's CI anchor job (run 38932582600) committed AnchorAdvanced for receipt-bound-delivery, giving anchor_run_id 38932582600.

Bug: merging main into PR #40's branch and running `vouch.lock merge-git-stages --root .vouch` (ours = the branch, theirs = main) replays main's 13 records, and the replayed head has anchor_run_id ''.

Cause, in store/merge.py merge_store_roots, replay path:
- _command_for_event(run_id=item.record.run_id) passes the source run id into AdvanceAnchor. But AnchorAdvanced carries no run id, and current = apply(current, decision.events) folds with no event_run_ids.
- build_event_records(ours, replayed_events, run_id=run_id) then envelopes every replayed event with the merge's own run id, which is '' locally.
- So every replayed CI-signed anchor loses its run claim.

Effect: the generated anchor plan re-anchors heads with an empty claim, so the next main CI run re-anchors the unit under a later run. The original CI provenance is erased, and until then check.evidence-anchors reports the unit NOT-CHECKED (anchor has no workflow run claim). This is not fail-open, but it rewrites history and makes merge direction matter.

Workaround used: merge in the other direction. Take main's store, then run `vouch.lock merge --root .vouch --other <branch store>`, so only the branch's local, claimless records are replayed.

Fix needs a D-26 decision and a frozen D-11 unit. Likely, a replayed event keeps its source record's run claim: per-event run ids through apply and build_event_records in the replay, with the merge record itself carrying the merge's run id. Alternatively, merge-git-stages could choose the side whose chain holds CI-claimed records as ours. Related: bd4.4.4, which covers anchors only advancing unclaimed heads.

description: Use the grill-with-docs decision-tree workflow to synthesize vouch mk2 internals, the existing vouch-mk2-system-diagram.html, mk1 lessons, and the adoption/implementation framework. Record settled domain language and hard-to-reverse architectural decisions, then revise the agreed system documentation only after the user confirms shared understanding.
design: Round 1 settled 2026-08-20: design an evolutionary target system with the proven mk2 assurance kernel and a product-owned adoption operating system; label implemented/piloted/proposed/adopter-owned/external elements. Beachhead is a technical lead or maintainer of a small agent-heavy GitHub team. Primary job is safer agent-assisted delivery; audit and standardization are secondary benefits. Scope is the full adoption lifecycle. Optimize brownfield-first with a greenfield fast lane. Preserve mk2's authority, purity, append-only history, content addressing, transition-gate, explicit-deviation, truthful-NOT_CHECKED, thin-adapter, and read-only-MCP principles; packaging, GitHub adapter, commands, schema and UI remain revisitable.
acceptance_criteria: All artifact-derived facts are reconciled; every reachable architecture, adoption, rollout, governance, and measurement decision branch is explicitly settled with the user; shared understanding is confirmed before edits; agreed documentation is updated and verified without overwriting unrelated work.
notes:
Rounds 1-8 are recorded in CONTEXT.md and prior bead history. Round 8 settled 2026-08-21: adoption-module failure cannot corrupt or reinterpret kernel results; health is recomputed locally without a daemon; event order is mechanical while unsupported wall-clock values remain claims; assessments are bounded and return incomplete on exhaustion; referenced history persists; notifications are local-only; enforcement outages never silently downgrade a hard gate. Round 9 settled 2026-08-21: preserve vouch-mk2-system-diagram.html; create vouch-system-diagram.html and vouch-optimal-system.md; show current, dogfooded, target, adopter-owned, and external-proof status honestly; document adoption and assurance as separate but composed flows; create only the agreed hard-to-reverse ADRs; verify the interactive diagram visually. Q74 settled 2026-08-21: optimal Vouch uses fail-closed hybrid incremental verification. Ordinary changes verify the affected closure from an exact verified baseline and reuse only locally stored results whose complete bound inputs are unchanged. Unmapped or global changes, missing or mismatched baselines, releases, recovery, upgrades, and explicit audits require full verification. Formal results are bound to exact Vouch, checker, model, and policy identity instead of rerunning for unrelated adopter code. No telemetry or remote cache is introduced. Canonical settled terms were added to CONTEXT.md. Q75-Q80 settled 2026-08-21: the per-scope reusable result is a verification capsule, distinct from the formal certificate. A human-confirmed scope manifest is authoritative; candidate automation may propose it but ambiguity fails closed. Capsules live only in the repository-local append-only content-addressed record and require an exact hard-gated baseline plus complete identity match; ephemeral caches cannot affect verdicts. The assurance kernel owns affected-closure planning, capsule validity, and composition; project policy declares scopes, dependencies, and commands; delivery adapters supply normalized change manifests and execute plans without deciding scope or claims. Incremental composition may support whole-project assurance when every scope and global obligation is accounted for, but reports distinguish it from full verification and expose baseline, head, affected/reused scopes, rationale, and last full revision. Ordinary cost scales with the affected closure; budget exhaustion is incomplete or NOT_CHECKED and blocks hard progression. CONTEXT.md was updated inline. Q81-Q88 settled 2026-08-21 with Q82 clarified by the user: release composition may use complete incremental composition, while full verification is triggered by global invalidation, missing trust, recovery, upgrades, audits, or declared cadence rather than every continuous-delivery release. Every relevant path has exactly one primary scope or explicit exclusion; purity versus effects changes dependency and integration obligations, not ownership. Shared behavior is modeled as its own primary scope, and effectful or cross-scope behavior as a first-class integration scope. Dependency contracts permit downstream reuse when unchanged; opaque dependencies conservatively propagate producer changes. The kernel independently binds adapter-supplied base, head, and path facts. Capsules bind all assurance inputs and identities semantically rather than expiring by time. Branch merges recompute closure from the exact common verified ancestor and never union green results blindly. The kernel emits immutable verification plans; local or delivery runner adapters may execute entries in parallel and return provenance-honest, plan-bound receipts. CONTEXT.md was updated inline. Q89-Q94 settled 2026-08-21: scope ownership remains path-level and single-primary-scope; independently governed behavior sharing a file belongs to a containing scope or should be split rather than introducing language-specific symbol ownership. The kernel is language-agnostic about purity and effects; mechanically produced effect facts may bind dependency contracts, but purity neither proves an unchanged contract nor does effectfulness imply global invalidation. Assurance policy limits full-verification distance by governed changes or releases, with projects able to tighten but not weaken tier requirements. Parallel plan attempts preserve all receipts; only complete successful scope execution creates a replacement capsule. Forge receipts bind exact change, plan, command, workflow/runner/toolchain, outcome, and output identity while reporting external attestation honestly and causing no Vouch telemetry. Full verification of all active scopes is distinct from a historical scrub of genesis-to-head events and evidence; incremental and full runs may validate a suffix from an exact verified checkpoint, while recovery, corruption, major upgrades, explicit history audits, and longer cadence trigger a historical scrub. CONTEXT.md was updated inline. Q95-Q102 settled 2026-08-21: a verified checkpoint binds exact history roots, state, schema, policy, verifier, and hard-gated repository revision and may extend only a trusted prefix through a verified suffix. Passed entries from a partial plan remain reusable only under the identical plan, tree, inputs, environment, and policy; retries append receipts and changes require a new plan. Ordinary incremental and full verification cover active scopes and claimed release rosters; historical scrubs cover retired and superseded history, and renewed old claims require current verification. Scope-manifest revisions are governed and use the union of impact under old and new mappings. Generated paths bind generator and inputs; vendored dependencies are explicit pinned scopes; exclusions cannot feed governed behavior. Cross-root consumers bind exact published dependency contracts and never share authority. Effectful scopes reuse only when effect inputs are fixed or mechanically bound; otherwise the relevant input and scope are volatile. Secret values are never stored or hashed; a non-secret version handle may be bound, otherwise execution remains volatile. CONTEXT.md was updated inline. Q103-Q109 settled 2026-08-21: greenfield projects establish a scope manifest, full verification, and historical scrub before reusable checkpoints; existing mk2 stores remain full-only after upgrade until human scope confirmation and explicit baseline establishment, with no synthesized retroactive capsules and permanent force-full availability. Retries are explicit, bounded, plan-identical, append-only, and visibly preserve instability. Incremental soundness is the central invariant: incremental composition never passes when full verification of the same supported state/change would fail; the bounded formal model and differential/property tests cover closure, capsules, checkpoints, invalidators, and merges. Performance promotion uses scaling shape and local declared budgets rather than a universal latency number. Claim boundaries state that Vouch cannot defeat an authority controlling repository, pinned executable, policy, runner, and credentials together. Roadmap: adoption/full foundations first, opt-in incremental dogfood second, default incremental only after equivalence/formal/migration/recovery/performance proof, with force-full retained. Add a fourth ADR for sound fail-closed incrementality and show incremental, full, historical-scrub, and baseline paths in the optimal diagram as target behavior. The decision frontier is empty pending final shared-understanding confirmation. CONTEXT.md was updated inline.

title: Record which tests each RED/GREEN ran (JUnit XML) and compare GREEN with RED
description: User decision 2026-11-22 (D-49 note). Report only, never a gate unless a later decision says so. The report is the runner's claim, like the exit status; claim-boundary must say so. title: Decide whether Vouch defends merge provenance against a hand-edited store
description: D-41 trusts origin, satisfied, generated and a merge record's heads as tool-written claims and refuses only what its general rule covers (D-41 notes of 2026-11-18). Known accepted forgeries with loss: (1) rewriting a marker's theirs_head to a later source head (no-op, drops the source's later work; needs no D-41 field); (2) a satisfied or origin entry naming a record held only by a third store; (3) a satisfied entry inside the claimed history for a fact the merge should have replayed. Reproductions: d41-forgery-loop_fable.OUT.md section 2; the review history: nested-merge-boundary_review2.OUT.md and recheck2-5. Decide the threat model first (who edits, who is harmed: solo developer, small team, CI). Candidate defence: a CI check at the pull-request boundary where both parent stores are available (d41-forgery-loop_fable.OUT.md section 4, option E). Not a defect of nested-merge-boundary@1. Further forged-provenance findings are appended here, not raised against a unit.
notes: User decision 2026-11-22 (on the owner's recommendation): option 2 plus option 1's docs. Threat model: a contributor whose changes reach the default branch through a pull request may hand-edit .vouch/; someone with direct push access to the default branch is out of scope and the docs say so. Defence: a CI check at the pull-request boundary that recomputes the merge from both parent stores (base and head) independently and fails if the committed store dropped or forged anything (d41-forgery-loop_fable.OUT.md section 4, option E). Covers the three known merge-provenance forgeries and the DEV-cc-02 forged merge transaction where reachable through a PR.
